claim_short: 15 imputed datasets averaged and rounded to one
reasons: the procedure is disclosed and reproduced in the script; averaging the m=15 completions into a single rounded dataset discards the between-imputation variance that multiple imputation exists to carry, so every interval downstream (including the bootstrap spread in C9 and C10) is conditioned on one imputed dataset. Not quantifiable here: the 15 individual completions were not supplied, only their rounded average

estimating a network over 20 nodes screens 190 node pairs per network and 380 across the two; the paper reports no p-value and applies no multiplicity control. Re-running the 190 pairwise polychoric tests per network: 128 (patrol) and 113 (detection) reach p<0.05 uncorrected against 9.5 expected by chance, falling to 73 and 74 under Bonferroni. Against a permutation max-statistic null (300 permutations, FWER threshold |r|=0.555 patrol / 0.819 detection) the lasso's 55 and 70 selected edges are a model-selection output, not a set of tests with a controlled error rate

the per-descriptor likelihood-ratio / delta-AIC values behind the screen are in electronic supplementary material S2-S3, which was not supplied, and the script records only the model formulas (clmm with and without a handler random intercept), not their output; an ordinal mixed model was not re-fitted here.
